principles.text: Re-up the foundations every 24 hours: sleep, morning sunlight, movement, nutrients and relationships.
View sunlight outdoors within 30-60 minutes of waking, longer if cloudy; windows and windshields filter out the effect.
Delay caffeine 90-120 minutes after waking and avoid it within 8-10 hours of bedtime.
Don't spike dopamine before or after effort; stacking stimulants lowers baseline. Learn to get dopamine from the effort itself.
Learning is two steps: focused attention triggers it, and the actual rewiring happens during sleep and NSDR.

sampleQA.question: I wake up around 3 am and can't fall back asleep. What should I change?

answer.text: Go to bed when you first feel sleepy. Pushing through that late-evening sleepiness is one reason people wake at 3 am.
Remove visible clocks, since checking the time trains your brain to keep waking then. Don't try hard to fall back asleep; use NSDR instead.
For middle-of-the-night waking, about 900 mg of myo-inositol can shorten the time it takes to fall back asleep.
If you wake to urinate, sip rather than gulp your last drink of the day and cut fluids 2-3 hours before bed.

sampleQA.question: How do I use cold exposure without hurting my strength gains?

answer.text: Aim for about 11 minutes of deliberate cold per week total, split into 2-4 sessions of 1-5 minutes, in water that's uncomfortably cold but safe.
Skip cold immersion in the ~4 hours after strength or hypertrophy training; do it before training or on a separate day.
Do it early in the day, not near bedtime, because the rebound rise in body temperature promotes wakefulness.
For metabolic benefit, end on cold and let your body rewarm on its own (the Søberg principle).

sampleQA.question: How do I stay motivated without crashing from stimulants and constant rewards?

answer.text: Big dopamine peaks drop your baseline afterward, so don't habitually stack pre-workout, music, phone and caffeine on the same effort.
Use random intermittent rewards: celebrate some wins, not every one, and tie the reward to the effort process.
Raise baseline with 10-30 minutes of morning sunlight and brief cold exposure, which gives a sustained rise rather than a crash.
For compulsive habits, a 30-60 day abstinence usually resets things; wait out the trough rather than re-stimulating.
